items.followUp: What is meant by effective nuclear charge?

rubric.why: Identifies the electrons responsible for the shielding effect.
rubric.description: States that inner-shell electrons repel outer-shell electrons.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying inner-shell electrons.

rubric.why: Explains the effect of shielding on outer-shell electrons.
rubric.description: States that shielding reduces the nuclear attraction experienced by outer-shell electrons.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the reduced nuclear attraction.

modelAnswer: The shielding effect is the repulsion of outer-shell electrons by inner-shell electrons.
It reduces the nuclear attraction experienced by outer-shell electrons.

rubric.why: Identifies Moseley’s change from arranging elements by atomic mass to arranging them by atomic number.
rubric.description: States that elements are arranged by increasing atomic number instead of atomic mass.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating the atomic-number basis in place of atomic mass.

rubric.why: States the revised periodic relationship based on Moseley’s work.
rubric.description: States that the properties of elements are periodic functions of their atomic numbers.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for giving the revised periodic law.

modelAnswer: Moseley arranged elements in increasing atomic number instead of atomic mass.
Thus, the properties of elements are periodic functions of their atomic numbers.
